title: The common-factor model
summary: CB-SEM explains the covariances among indicators by a few common factors plus unique errors, and estimates the parameters that make the implied covariance matrix closest to the observed one.

body.text: In CB-SEM each reflective indicator is a weighted common factor plus a unique error. The model implies a covariance matrix for the indicators, and estimation chooses the parameters that bring this implied matrix as close as possible to the sample covariance matrix S (Bollen 1989).

body.explanation: Λ holds the loadings, Φ the variances and covariances of the factors, Θ the unique (error) variances; θ collects all free parameters. With structural paths, Φ is itself a function of the paths and disturbance variances.

body.caption: A two-factor CFA: each indicator loads on one factor; the factors covary.

body.text: Because unique variance is separated from the factors, factor correlations and structural paths are not attenuated by random measurement error, provided the model is correct. And because the model restricts S (here 36 variances and covariances are reproduced by 17 parameters), the restrictions can be tested: that is global fit (lesson 5.4). In the two-factor example the estimated factor correlation is .287.
SEM Lab's CB engine estimates reflective (common-factor) constructs only; composite-formative blocks are rejected with an explanation rather than silently treated as factors.

mistake.title: Treating a sum score as the factor
mistake.text: The mean of a scale's items still contains measurement error; the factor in a CFA does not. Correlations of sum scores are therefore smaller than factor correlations, and the two must not be mixed in one comparison.

tryIt.task: Run CB-SEM (ML) on this two-factor model and read the standardised loadings, the unique variances and the factor correlation.

checks.question: In Σ(θ) = ΛΦΛ′ + Θ, what does Θ contain?

options.text: The unique (error) variances of the indicators, and any error covariances you specify

options.feedback: Factor variances and covariances are in Φ.
Paths enter through Φ (via the structural equations), not Θ.

checks.explanation: Λ loadings, Φ factors, Θ uniquenesses.

checks.question: Why can a CFA be tested against the data?

options.text: Because it reproduces many variances and covariances with fewer parameters, which imposes restrictions the data can violate.
options.feedback: Correct. The degrees of freedom count those restrictions.

options.text: Because its estimates are always significant.
options.feedback: Significance of parameters is a different question from whether the model reproduces the covariances.
The χ² test of fit is an analytic likelihood-ratio test, not a bootstrap.
